title: Prior-session-high break and retest on 15m: volume-backed break, buy the bullish wick back into the level
rule_summary: Chart 15m, closed bars, UTC; signal at bar close, fill at next open. SESSIONS: three 8-hour blocks per UTC day, 00:00-07:45, 08:00-15:45, 16:00-23:45 (32 bars each). LEVEL: PSH = highest high of the previous completed session. BREAK: in the current session, the first bar b whose close >= 1.002*PSH and whose volume >= 1.5 x mean volume of bars b-20..b-1 (activity filter b). RETEST WINDOW: bars b+1..b+16 (4 h; may run into the next session). RETEST BAR t: low(t) <= 1.002*PSH AND close(t) >= PSH AND close(t) > open(t) (a wick into the level, closing back above it). INVALIDATION: any close < 0.995*PSH after b and before t cancels the setup. ENTRY: at the first retest bar, buy at the next open E. One setup per session, one position per pair. STOP: min(0.998*low(t), 0.99*E), fixed at entry and executed intrabar, so it is always at least 1% below entry. TARGET: E*1.02. TIME EXIT: 48 bars (12 h) after entry. No higher-timeframe filter, same numbers on all pairs.
mechanism: Break-and-retest (TradeZella playbook, standard price-action practice): after a prior session's high breaks on volume, resting sell orders above it are absorbed and stopped-out shorts turn buyers. The first pullback tests whether breakout buyers defend the level (role reversal). Entering on a bullish close that wicks into the level puts the stop just under the defended level instead of chasing the break candle, which is where straight breakouts (H-002, I-093) lose to noise and cost. Counterparty: traders fading the breakout and late sellers on the pullback, whose stops sit above the new intraday high. Move per trade: stop at least 1% and target 2%, so exits are 1-2% away; a 45% hit rate plus time exits gives about +0.5% gross, above the 0.30% round trip.
